Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Recap: rate & quota requirements for Acme Health — next steps

Hi Alice & Dave,

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to learn more about Acme Health's inference footprint. Below is a concise recap of the pain points, our shared goals, and proposed next steps. Please flag any inaccuracies.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Unpredictable token costs due to bursty traffic from batch jobs and patient-facing webhooks.
- Need strict per-customer quotas and per-org routing (different SLAs for partners vs internal apps).
- Current stack (K8s + API gateway + Redis) lacks an easy way to enforce per-customer token budgets without custom middleware.

Success criteria (what you said would make this a win):
1) Enforce hard per-customer monthly token limits + soft per-minute rate protections to prevent noisy neighbors.
2) Route requests to higher-cost models only for priority customers while falling back to cheaper variants elsewhere.
3) Stay within a 25% budgeted token spend reduction target in 3 months after rollout.
4) Maintain P95 tail latency <= 300ms for interactive flows.

What we proposed on the call:
- Redwood can implement per-customer quotas and hierarchical tiering (partner/internal/dev tiers) with circuit-breaker fallbacks.
- Policy-based routing to model variants (high-accuracy vs quantized) with automatic fallback during capacity constraints.
- Prefill a minimal MAP (mutual action plan) and a short technical appendix mapping to your K8s+Redis architecture.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- Ben: Send a one-page MAP and security overview (attached) — today.
- Monica: Prep a short demo of tiered routing and quota enforcement (sandbox) — target 4/22.
- Alice: Share a small sample of traffic patterns and one typical slow query window (for quantization profiling) — by 4/21.

Attachments: MAP-AcmeHealth-v0.1.pdf (draft), redwood-security-summary.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the sandbox demo next week.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

2) The 25% spend reduction is a target we discussed internally; if Redwood can show a path with conservative assumptions that reaches ~15% in 90 days and 25% with caching/kv optimizations, that'll be compelling.

I'll pull together a 48-hour trace/sample and upload to the Drive link you provided by EOD 4/21. Also looping in Dave in case he wants to weigh in on the priority routing constraints.

- We absolutely need API-key-scoped quotas; we have per-customer billing units and partner accounts that require separate caps.
- Any solution that requires heavy client-side changes will be a lower priority; we prefer server-side policies or an ingress-side plugin.

Dave — short answer: yes.

We have two options for enforcement in your stack:
1) Ingress filter (Envoy/NGINX): lightweight Envoy filter we can provide for key-based quota checks and routing. This keeps all enforcement out of your app code.
2) Redwood sidecar (optional): deploys alongside the model-serving pods and enforces policies with tighter cache locality — more complex but lower latency for KV-heavy workloads.

For the demo on 4/22 we'll show option (1) in a staging cluster so you can validate with minimal changes. We'll also include a short checklist for mapping API keys to billing accounts.

I'll attach a small snippet of the Envoy filter and confirmation steps after the demo.

Thanks — Monica
